description: Calendar definition validation: every error code of chronology-engine.md §11, root-cause reporting, and valid edge cases. Starts from the baseline of invalid-definitions.json.
verification: Each case changes the baseline by hand; the expected errors follow from the rule quoted in its note (chronology-engine.md §3, §11).

cases.note: level ids are unique; nothing else is checked when levels are invalid
level ids match ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$ (a schema violation with a dedicated code; semantic checks such as the month template now naming an unknown level do not run)
'intercalary' is reserved
at most 20 levels (schema maxItems with a dedicated code)
the template's level must exist
a month's children must be day templates
explicit reference to a missing template
a run without template uses the child level's default_template, which is not set
the same run is valid once the level has a default_template
counts are ≥ 1 (a schema violation with a dedicated code)
level-0 templates are uniform
level-0 units contain base units, not templates
only named slots can be intercalary
counts have at most 1000 digits
cycle_excluded refers to cycles of the regime
the pattern's templates are year templates
every pattern template exists
exception templates exist
the alignment cannot be a date of the calendar being defined
fields go from the top level down without gaps
the year is a number
months have 10 days
field keys are level ids
the cycle's level exists
the reset level is coarser than the cycle's level
reset cycles need no anchor date
a continuous cycle needs an anchor date
index < length
the anchor date is a unit of the cycle's level
regime 0 has no previous regime to continue
an intercalary slot excluded from a cycle of the regime is valid
cycle ids are unique within a regime
the anchor unit must not be excluded from its cycle (here its month is)
a continuous cycle continues the previous regime's sequence
the previous regime has no such cycle
the continued cycle has the same length
only continuous cycles continue across regimes
a continued cycle adds no error when the previous regime is invalid: root cause only
regime ids are unique
every regime after the first has a start
regime starts are strictly increasing
a local start is accepted (resolved with the compiled structure, #14)
the first era starts at -infinity
later eras have a start
era ids are unique
local anchors use astronomical years (no era)
a local era start is accepted (resolved with the compiled structure, #14)
a non-local era start needs a resolved moment
phase starts increase
the first phase starts at 0
phase starts are < 1
overlay ids are unique
format keys are level ids of the calendar
braces must be balanced ({{ and }} are literal braces)
intercalary formats are checked too
every token kind of chronology-engine.md §3.11 is accepted
other schema violations are schema.invalid at the offending member
a broken template stops the regime's dependent checks: no alignment error
independent errors are all reported
